opportunities.title: Qiuyue (Shirley) Xue
opportunities.description: I’m an assistant professor in the Department of Computer Science at Purdue University , leading the Snowball Lab . I’m also a visiting faculty researcher at Google . I received my Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from the University of Washington, advised by Shwetak Patel and Vikram Iyer . During my PhD, I have interned at Microsoft Research, Apple AI/ML, and Google Health. I got my B.S in Computer Science and B.S. in Electrical Engineering from Peking University, and M.S. in Computer Science from Georgia Institute of Technology. I’m broadly interested in Ubiquitous Computing, Human–Computer Interaction, Wearables, Computing for Health, and novel Sensing Techniques. My recent work focuses on advancing the wearable space by transforming everyday accessories into low-power, intelligent systems that enable applications previously difficult or impossible to achieve. These applications span health, well-being, and human–computer interaction. I will be recruiting PhD students this application cycle . If you’re interested in working with me, feel free to contact me with your CV.

opportunities.description: School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, I am looking for self-motivated PhD students with cs/ee/math/statistics backgrounds joining my group at Oregon State University on reinforcement learning and information retrieval. If you are interested, please apply to our CS or AI degree program and mention my name in your application. Remote internship positions are also available. Prospective students may contact me (huazhengwang at gmail.com) with your CV and transcripts. Dr. Huazheng Wang is an Assistant Professor in the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) at Oregon State University. He was a postdoctoral research associate at Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at Princeton University, hosted by Dr. Mengdi Wang . He received his PhD in Computer Science from University of Virginia in 2021 supervised by Dr. Hongning Wang , and his B.E. from University of Science and Technology of China in 2015. His research interests include machine learning, reinforcement learning, information retrieval and data mining. His recent works focused on developing efficient and robust reinforcement learning and multi-armed bandit algorithms with applications to online recommendation and ranking systems. He has received the best paper award at SIGIR 2019 and Bloomberg Data Science PhD Fellowship.

opportunities.title: Ghada Almashaqbeh
opportunities.description: I am an assistant professor in the School of Computing at UConn. I am also affiliated with the Connecticut Advanced Computing Center (CACC) and the Engineering for Human Rights Initiative. Before joining UConn, I spent a while exploring the entrepreneurship world. I cofounded CacheCash, a startup that came out of my PhD thesis, and I was a Cryptographer at NuCypher. Also, I was an advisor for the Melon and Sunscreen, a 2023 Foresight Institute fellow, and a 2023 TLDR fellow at Uniswap Foundation. I received my PhD in Computer Science from Columbia University in 2019, where I was a member of the Cryptography Lab and the Data Science Institute. During the PhD, I was fortunate to have Allison Bishop and Tal Malkin as my advisors. My research interests span cryptography, systems security, and privacy, with a primary focus on distributed cryptographic protocols, privacy-preserving computing, and blockchain-based systems. A central theme of my work is bridging theory and practice; I design secure and efficient systems and protocols that connect rigorous cryptographic foundations with real-world applications, particularly in decentralized and heterogeneous settings.

opportunities.title: Andrew Head
opportunities.description: Students + applicants: please read these FAQs before emailing me My lab does research in human-computer interaction with an emphasis on tools for thought. Broadly, my group tackles information-intensive technical tasks, often involving formalism. We give users tools to digest and make progress amidst high complexity. Currently, we are developing tools to improve math explanation, computer-assisted proof, code understanding and verification, forecasting, and scientific reasoning. Our group specializes in qualitative and technical HCI methods. On the one hand, we conduct qualitative studies with expert users that give a detailed picture of work. For example, our recent studies have provided rich inventories of the user experience of using proof assistants , verifying code with property-based testing , and writing accessible mathematical explanations .

opportunities.description: The Human Centric Technology & Design Lab (HCT Design Lab) applies a human-centered design approach and emerging technologies to promote health and wellness and enhance user experiences, advancing design research and education within the community. Our mission is to advance human-centered technology and design by integrating emerging technologies with a deep understanding of user needs. We prioritize health, wellness, and enhanced user experiences through a holistic, interdisciplinary approach that emphasizes usability studies, user-centered design, and universal design principles. By fostering an inclusive design research and education community, we strive to create innovative solutions that are accessible, functional, and beneficial for all, promoting equitable user experiences across many populations. Through rigorous research and collaboration, we aim to shape the future of design for the betterment of society. Essential supplies and materials for design and research

When considering which psychology professor from Stanford University will be accepting PhD students, it is essential to research faculty members whose research interests align with your own. Stanford’s Psychology Department boasts a diverse range of experts, from cognitive and social psychology to developmental and clinical psychology. opportunities.title: Yale University
opportunities.description: Home » News » We're recruiting new PhD students! The Social Robotics Lab is very interested in recruiting new PhD students. Our lab is in the Computer Science department within the School of Engineering and Applied Sciences at Yale, and does work in robotics, human-robot interaction, and machine learning. There are few jobs that allow you to work on whatever you want to work on, pioneer you own projects, and investigate the cutting edge of human-robot interaction; this one fulfills all three. If any of this sounds interesting at all, please apply this fall! You are also invited to email the current grad students with any and all questions ( http://scazlab.yale.edu/people/graduate-students ). We explore human behavior and how robotics can improve human lives. A lot of the work is in the realm of socially assistive robotics and developmental robotics. We are interdisciplinary and incorporate knowledge from the fields of robotics, psychology, mathematics (machine learning), and computer science. Our projects range from robots that assist in collaborative manufacturing (intelligently offering you a screwdriver the moment you need it), to robots that can intelligently use nonverbal behavior in collaboration, to robots that act as personalized math tutors to 5th grade kids, to robots that aid in the social skill development in children with autism. We encourage you to read more about our current projects on our website- http://scazlab.yale.edu/yale-social-robotics-lab-research-projects .

opportunities.title: About
opportunities.description: I’m an incoming assistant professor at UC Berkeley, where I’ll be a member of the Department of Statistics and an affiliate with EECS , starting in Fall 2027. I work on building tools to understand and improve the implicit world models of generative models in AI. Part of my work also involves integrating insights from the behavioral sciences into the development of AI systems like large language models. I study these problems both in traditional AI domains and in the social sciences. I’m currently a postdoctoral fellow with the Harvard Data Science Initiative at Harvard University and the Bike Shop at MIT. I completed my PhD in computer science at Columbia University, where I was advised by David Blei . Before that, I received a BA in computer science and statistics from Harvard University. During my PhD, I was an NSF GRFP Fellow and also interned at Google AI and Facebook AI Research. Upon graduating, I received the Morton B. Friedman Memorial Prize for excellence in engineering. Here is my curriculum vitae . Here is a video I recorded about the methods I’ve worked on to test AI’s implicit world models, and here are articles from the Wall Street Journal and Quanta Magazine about this work.

opportunities.description: Students choose to pursue a doctorate degree for all different reasons. Some students want to progress in their career. opportunities.title: Best Jobs for College Students | ScholarshipOwl
opportunities.description: When most people think about working in college, they imagine themselves living off financial aid and the minimum wage work they can get from a fast food joint. You are obviously more than welcome to do so if you want, but chances are you will need more than a pint-sized paycheck and scholarship money to get by. Before you go end up broke trying to start your future, you may want to learn about the high paying career opportunities that are available to students right now. Here is a list of the six jobs students should consider to make some extra cash. Most internships do not offer any money, but learning how to find an internship can offer financial compensation for career training. In other words, you could lean more about your career path while simultaneously making money. This will make it easier for you to find work after graduation and help you avoid massive debt living on student loans. If you happen to establish some positive career connections, you might be able to land a job before completing your degree program. As a freelance writer, you can work from the comfort of your own home and make a decent salary too. Every word on the web (including this one) has to be written by someone, and a lot of companies will pay people to write those words for them. Most freelance writers start at about $15 an hour, whereas experienced writers can make as much as $50 or more an hour.

opportunities.title: Why and how to email faculty prior to applying to graduate school — Luck Lab
opportunities.description: [Note: Our experience is in Psychology and Neuroscience, but this probably applies to most other disciplines.] It is now the season for students in the U.S. to begin the stressful, arduous, and sometimes expensive process of applying to PhD programs. One common piece of advice (that we give our own students) is to send emails to faculty at the institutions where you plan to apply. In this blog post, we explain why this is a good thing to do and how to do it. Some students find it very stressful to send these emails, and we hope that the “how to do it” section will make it less stressful. You don’t have to email the faculty, but it can be extremely helpful, and we strongly recommend that you do it. In many programs (especially in Psychology), individual faculty play a huge role in determining which students are accepted into the PhD program. In these programs, students are essentially accepted into the lab of a specific faculty member, and the faculty are looking for students who have the knowledge, skills, and interests to succeed in their labs. This is often called the “apprenticeship model.”
